statements.claim: Uddhava had served Krishna since he was five years old and had grown old in that service.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.1-2: 'yaḥ pañca-hāyano mātrā prātar-āśāya yācitaḥ / sa kathaṃ sevayā tasya kālena jarasaṃ gataḥ' (serving him, he grew old in time).

statements.claim: Vidura asked Uddhava to speak of Krishna, and Uddhava sat for a moment silent, sunk in the sweetness of Krishna's feet, limbs trembling, tears falling, then wiped his eyes and smiled.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.3-5: 'sa muhūrtam abhūt tūṣṇīṃ kṛṣṇāṅghri-sudhayā... pulakodbhinna-sarvāṅgo muñcan mīlad-dṛśā śucaḥ / śanakair... punar āgataḥ'; pack excerpt: wiping his eyes he smiled.

statements.claim: Uddhava lamented that the sun (Krishna) had set, that he had no good news for houses stripped of fortune, and that the world was wretched, more so the Yadavas who dwelt with Hari and never knew him.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.6-7 pack rendering: 'The sun Krishna has set; what good news can I tell in homes bereft of fortune? Wretched is this world, and more so the Yadavas, who dwelt with Hari and knew him not.' Sanskrit: 'durbhago bata loko 'yaṃ yadavo nitarām api'.

statements.claim: The Yadavas were masters at reading a glance, mature in counsel, devoted to Krishna alone, yet the Lord's own maya had closed their eyes.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.8-9: 'iṅgita-jñāḥ puru-prauḍhā ekārāmāś ca sātvatāḥ / devasya māyayā spṛṣṭāḥ'.

statements.claim: At the Rajasuya of Yudhishthira the three worlds looked upon Krishna and their eyes were blessed.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.12: 'yad dharma-sūnor bata rājasūye nirīkṣya dṛk-svastyayanaṃ tri-lokaḥ' (dharma-sūnu = Yudhishthira).

statements.claim: Krishna's loving laughing glance in the rasa play gave worth to all it fell on.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.13: 'yasyānurāga-pluta-hāsa-rāsa-līlāvaloka-pratilabdha-mānāḥ'.

statements.claim: At that same Rajasuya even Shishupala, who hated Krishna all his life, reached perfection through that hatred.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.18: 'dṛṣṭā bhavadbhir nanu rājasūye caidyasya kṛṣṇaṃ dviṣato 'pi siddhiḥ'; 'fixed gazing' gloss is traditional (Shishupala's meditation on Krishna in enmity).

statements.claim: In the great battles, heroes of the earth fell gazing on the lotus of Krishna's face.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.19: 'tathaiva cānye nara-loka-vīrā ya āhave kṛṣṇa-mukhāravindam'.

statements.claim: Uddhava spoke of the Unborn Lord's birth-play in Vasudeva's house and of how Krishna, bowing at his parents' feet, had spoken to them.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.15-16: 'ajasya janma-viḍambanaṃ yad vasudeva-gehe' and 'yad āha pādāv abhivandya pitroḥ'.

statements.claim: Uddhava told Vidura he was no ordinary minister but one without equal, a lord of the three worlds whose every desire was fulfilled by the fortune of his own sovereignty.
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.20: 'svayaṃ tv asāmyātiśayas tryadhīśaḥ svārājya-lakṣmy-āpta-samasta-kāmaḥ'.

statements.claim: Vidura had come to the bank of the Yamuna to learn from Uddhava the deeds of Krishna.
statements.evidence: Pack index entry: characters Uddhava/Vidura, location 'the bank of the Yamuna'; canonical event evt_0537 frames Vidura hearing Uddhava's lament.

statements.claim: The river that flowed past them was the same water that had once carried the little boat of the cowherd boy's infancy.
statements.evidence: Closing lyrical image tying the Yamuna to Krishna's infancy; the pack's BP 3.2.1-20 contains no infancy-boat motif (the Yamuna infancy crossing belongs to the earlier Vasudeva episode of the corpus), so the concrete 'boat' image is an atmospheric flourish rather than a pack-supported event.

notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. One connective-narration question: the final image of the Yamuna having 'carried the little boat of the cowherd boy's infancy' is an invented concrete detail (no boat motif in the infancy tradition the pack draws on); kept as atmosphere, flagged for possible rewrite to the pack-grounded crossing image.

statements.claim: Arjuna found the bodies of Krishna and Balarama and performed the funeral rites for them and for all the slain.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'ARJUNA having found the bodies of Krishńa and of Ráma, performed for them, and the rest of the slain, the obsequial rites.'

statements.claim: The eight queens of Krishna, Rukmini at their head, embraced the body of Hari and entered the funeral fire; Revati held the corpse of Rama on the blazing pile, which was cool to her.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'The eight queens of Krishńa... with Rukminí at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire. Revatí also, embracing the corpse of Ráma, entered the blazing pile, which was cool to her, happy in contact with her lord.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena, and Vasudeva with Devaki and Rohini, gave themselves to the flames.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'Ugrasena and Anakadundubhi [Vasudeva], with Devakí and Rohiní, committed themselves to the flames.'

statements.claim: Arjuna made the people leave the city, took Vajra, and led the thousands of Krishna's widowed wives out of Dwaraka slowly and with tenderness, the city following.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'Arjuna... made all the people leave the city, and took Vajra with him... conducted the thousands of the wives of Krishńa, with Vajra, and all the people, from Dwáraká, with tenderness and care, and travelled slowly away.'

statements.claim: Behind them the sea rose and swallowed Dwaraka, leaving only the dwelling of the deity of the Yadu race; the ocean has never washed it away, Kesava still abides there, and whoever visits that holy shrine is freed of his sins.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwáraká, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu. The sea has not yet been able to wash that temple away, and there Keśava constantly abides... Whoever visits that holy shrine... is liberated from all his sins.'

statements.claim: On the same day Hari departed from the earth, the dark-bodied Kali age descended.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'on the same day that Hari departed from the earth the powerful dark-bodied Kali age descended.'

statements.claim: The Sudharman palace and the Parijata tree, which Krishna had brought down from heaven, went back to heaven.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'The Sudharman palace and the Párijáta tree, which had been brought to earth by Krishńa, both proceeded to heaven.'

statements.claim: Arjuna halted the column in the country of Panchanada, a rich and fertile spot, and robbers, coveting the widowed women and wealth, assembled the villainous Abhiras.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'Arjuna, halted the people... in the Panchanada country, in a rich and fertile spot; but the desires of the robbers... were excited, when they observed so many widowed females, also such great riches... they assembled the villainous Ábhiras.'

statements.claim: The robbers taunted that Arjuna, rich and guarded only by husband-slain women, was a disgrace to brave men, his pride swollen from slaying Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha and Karna, and urged the villagers to take their long thick staves.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'Here is this Arjuna, immensely rich, and having numerous women, whose husbands have been slain... His pride is raised by the death of Bhíshma, Drońa, Jayadratha, Karńa... Up, up; take your long thick staves.'

statements.claim: They rushed with cudgels and clods of earth; Arjuna derided them — 'Retire, wretches, ignorant of what is right, unless you are eager to die' — but they seized his treasure and his women.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'they rushed, armed with cudgels and clods of earth... Arjuna... said to them in derision, "Retire, wretches, ignorant of what is right, unless ye are desirous of dying." But they disregarded his menaces, and seized his treasures and his women.'

statements.claim: Gandiva would not tighten — the string stayed slack — the incantations of the superhuman weapons would not return, his arrows only scratched the herdsmen, Agni's arrows were themselves destroyed and fatal to him, and the might of Krishna could not be recalled, so arrows flew at random or were brushed aside.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'he began to brace his heavenly bow Gándíva... it continued flaccid: neither could he call to recollection the incantations of the superhuman weapons... merely scratched the skin. The arrows given him by Agni to carry certain destruction now were themselves destroyed, and were fatal to Arjuna... now they were put aside by the peasants, or they flew at random.' Khandava provenance of Agni's gift is the standard context for the Agni-given arrows.

statements.claim: With his quiver empty Arjuna beat the bandits with the horn of his bow and they laughed, then carried off all the women of the Vrishni and Andhaka tribes.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'His arrows being expended, he beat the banditti with the horn of his bow; but they only laughed at his blows: and the barbarians... carried off all the women of the Vrishńi and Andhaka tribes.'

statements.claim: Arjuna cried 'Alas, alas, I am deserted by my lord!', and in that instant the bow, heavenly arms, chariot and steeds perished, like a donation to an unlearned Brahman; he lamented that fate had laid feebleness on him, and that without that righteous aid he was overcome by peasants.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'exclaiming, Alas! alas! I am deserted by my lord!... in that instant the bow and heavenly arms, his car and steeds, perished entirely, like a donation to an unlearned Brahman... "Resistless," said he, "are the decrees of fate... The valour of Arjuna, the strength of Bhíma, was all his work; and without him I am overcome by peasants."'

statements.claim: Arjuna went to Mathura and installed Vajra as king, then found Vyasa living in a wood, saluted him prostrate, and Vyasa asked how he came to be shorn of his lustre.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'Arjuna went to the city of Mathurá, and there installed the Yádava prince, Vajra, as its king. There he beheld Vyása, who was living in a wood... The Muni surveyed him for some time, as he lay prostrate at his feet, and said to him, "How is it that I see you thus shorn of your lustre?"'

notes: Close paraphrase of Vishnu Purana 5.38 throughout (incl. robbers' taunt, Gandiva failing, lament, Mathura/Vyasa scene). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED; only devotional connective framing (Kali age 'taking the strength of the strongest man alive') which does not assert pack-contradicting facts.

statements.claim: One hundred and twenty-five years after Krishna descended into the Yadu line, the gods came to Dwaraka to ask him to return to his abode.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, BP 11.6.24-30: 'A hundred and twenty-five years have passed since you descended in the Yadu line... If you think fit, return to your supreme abode.'

statements.claim: Brahma spoke for the assembled gods, with Shiva among them.
statements.evidence: BP 11.6: speech headed 'śrī-brahmovāca'; pack index characters: Krishna, Brahma, Shiva, the gods.

statements.claim: Brahma said dharma had been established among the good who keep their word, and that Krishna had descended into the Yadu line bearing a peerless form.
statements.evidence: BP 11.6.21-22: 'dharmaś ca sthāpitaḥ satsu satya-sandheṣu vai tvayā / avatīrya yador vaṃśe bibhrad rūpam anuttamam'.

statements.claim: Brahma said the virtuous men of the Kali age would tell of Krishna's deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 11.6.23: 'yāni te caritānīśa manuṣyāḥ sādhavaḥ kalau'.

statements.claim: Brahma said Krishna's work for the gods was all but done, the clan was nearly destroyed by the brahmins' curse, and he should return to his supreme abode if he thought fit.
statements.evidence: BP 11.6.25-26: 'nādhunā te 'khilādhāra deva-kāryāvaśeṣitam / tataḥ sva-dhāma paramaṃ viśasva yadi manyase'; pack excerpt adds the brahmins'-curse clause.

statements.claim: Krishna answered that the earth's burden was indeed lifted but the Yadava clan had grown proud — swollen with valour, prowess and splendour — and could not be left standing; its destruction, born of the brahmins' curse, had already begun, and he would go when it had run its course.
statements.evidence: BP 11.6.28-30: 'tad idaṃ yādava-kulaṃ vīrya-śaurya-śriyoddhatam... idānīṃ nāśa ārabdhaḥ kulasya dvija-śāpa-jaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna answered that the earth's burden was indeed lifted and he would go at the end of the curse.'

statements.claim: Brahma and the gods took leave of Dwaraka, and the hour of Krishna's leaving was fixed by the slow work of the curse.
statements.evidence: Inference from BP 11.6.28-31 (Krishna will depart once the curse's destruction is complete); pack passage ends at śrī-śuka uvāca (v.31) without detailing the gods' departure, so the 'appointment hanging over Dwaraka' is narrative framing consistent with the exchange.

notes: Faithful rendering of BP 11.6.19-31 dialogue. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. Inner reflections (lamp waiting for its oil, curse as mechanism of release) are interpretive but do not assert sourceable facts against the pack.

statements.claim: The hunter Jara, whose arrow had struck Krishna's foot, was told by Krishna: 'Fear not; rise. This was my own doing. Go, with my leave, to the abode of the virtuous.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, BP 11.30.38-39: 'Krishna said to Jara: "Fear not; rise. This was my own doing. Go, with my leave, to the abode of the virtuous."'

statements.claim: Daruka, whom Krishna had sent away, searched for his master's path and found him at the root of an ashvattha tree, surrounded by the blazing divine weapons of Vishnu, and fell weeping at his feet.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.39-41: 'ity ādiṣṭo bhagavatā kṛṣṇenecchā-śarīriṇā / dārukaḥ kṛṣṇa-padavīm anvicchann adhigamya tām / taṃ tatra tigma-dyubhir āyudhair vṛtaṃ hy aśvattha-mūle kṛta-ketanaṃ patim / sneha-plutātmā nipapāta pādayo rathād avaplutya sa-bāṣpa-locanaḥ'.

statements.claim: Daruka lamented that without Krishna's lotus feet his sight had perished and entered into darkness.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.42: 'apaśyatas tvac-caraṇāmbujaṃ prabho dṛṣṭiḥ praṇaṣṭā tamasi praviṣṭā'.

statements.claim: While Daruka spoke, the chariot bearing the Garuda banner and the divine weapons of Vishnu rose and followed Krishna out of the world.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.43-44: 'iti bruvati sūte vai ratho garuḍa-lāñchanaḥ / tam anvagacchan divyāni viṣṇu-praharaṇāni ca'.

statements.claim: Krishna sent Daruka to Dwaraka with the message: tell the kinsmen of their mutual destruction and of Balarama's departure and of his own state; none should stay in Dwaraka; all should take their possessions and, with Arjuna's help, go to Indraprastha, for the sea would soon flood the city.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.45-47: 'gaccha dvāravatīṃ sūta jñātīnāṃ nidhanaṃ mithaḥ / dvārakāyāṃ ca na stheyaṃ bhavadbhiś ca sva-bandhubhiḥ / svaṃ svaṃ parigrahaṃ sarve ādāya...'; pack excerpt adds 'of Balarama's departure and of my state... with Arjuna's help, go to Indraprastha. The sea will soon flood the city I have left.'

statements.claim: Krishna counselled Daruka: hold to my dharma, be firm in knowledge, indifferent and unshaken, seeing all things as one.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.48: 'tvaṃ tu mad-dharmam āsthāya jñāna-niṣṭha upekṣakaḥ'; 'pairs of opposites / seeing all as one' is a standard gloss of upekṣaka-jñāna-niṣṭha.

statements.claim: Daruka circumambulated his master, bowed again and again, and went on his way to Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: BP 11.30.49: 'ity uktas taṃ parikramya namaskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ'.

notes: Faithful to BP 11.30.38-49. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. The hunter's trembling and the final lyrical passage ('the stillest figure in the world... the last departure no messenger could carry') are connective atmosphere consistent with the pack.

statements.claim: The ancestors (Pitris), Siddhas, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas and great serpents came, eager to witness the Lord's departure, and their celestial cars crowded the heavens.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.1-3: 'pitaraḥ siddha-gandharvā vidyādhara-mahoragāḥ / draṣṭu-kāmā bhagavato niryāṇaṃ paramotsukāḥ / vavṛṣuḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi vimānāvalibhir nabhaḥ'.

statements.claim: Flowers rained down and the drums of heaven sounded on their own.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.3 & 6: 'vavṛṣuḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi...' and 'divi dundubhayo neduḥ petuḥ sumanasaś ca khāt'.

statements.claim: The hunter Jara, terrified and certain he had wronged Krishna, had seen a man in yellow robes rapt in yoga and endued with many arms, and Krishna comforted him and sent him away before he could finish asking forgiveness.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Jara beheld a man dressed in yellow robes, rapt in Yoga and endued with many arms. Regarding himself an offender, and filled with fear, he touched the feet of Keshava. The high-souled one comforted him and then ascended upwards'; BP 11.30 (pack for DKS_0531) has Krishna bless Jara and send him to the abode of the virtuous.

statements.claim: Seeing Brahma before him, Krishna gathered his opulences back into himself and closed his lotus eyes.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.4-5: 'bhagavān pitāmahaṃ vīkṣya vibhūtīr ātmano vibhuḥ / lokābhirāmāṃ sva-tanuṃ dhāraṇā-dhyāna-maṅgalam'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna, seeing Brahma, gathered his opulences into himself, closed his lotus eyes.'

statements.claim: The fire of yoga rose from within him and consumed his body, and when the gods looked again there was nothing beneath the tree.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, BP 11.31.1-8: 'consumed his body with the fire of yoga, and entered his own abode, while the gods, amazed, could not trace his path.'

statements.claim: Even the gods headed by Brahma could not trace where he had gone — like lightning, which once it leaves its cloud no one can say where it has gone.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.7-8: 'devādayo brahma-mukhyā na viśantaṃ sva-dhāmani / saudāmanyā yathāklāśe yāntyā hitvābhra-maṇḍalam' (lightning simile is direct).

statements.claim: The Mahabharata's telling has Krishna rise filling the whole vault of heaven with splendour, with Indra, the twin Ashvinis, Rudra and the Adityas advancing to receive him.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'ascended upwards, filling the entire welkin with splendour. When he reached Heaven, Vasava and the twin Ashvinis and Rudra and the Adityas... advanced to receive him.'

statements.claim: The earth would feel his absence in the city by the sea, in the women he left there, and in the sea itself.
statements.evidence: Closing atmosphere anticipating the following episodes (flood of Dwaraka, widows' departure); no factual assertion beyond the pack's own sequel events.

notes: Faithful synthesis of BP 11.31.1-8 and MBh 16.4 (explicitly presented as two tellings of the same moment). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Daruka came to Dwaraka and told Vasudeva and Ugrasena of the complete destruction of the Vrishnis/Yadavas, and that Krishna and Balarama were gone.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.14-15: 'dāruko dvārakām etya vasudevograsenayoḥ / kathayām āsa nidhanaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa'; the 'gone' content follows from the family giving up life 'bhagavad-virahāturāḥ' (11.31.16-18).

statements.claim: Devaki, Rohini and Vasudeva, seeing neither Krishna nor Balarama, gave up their lives in grief.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.16-18: 'devakī rohiṇī caiva vasudevas tathā sutau / prāṇāṃś ca vijahus tatra bhagavad-virahāturāḥ'. (The story follows the BP reading over VP 5.38's 'committed themselves to the flames' — the pack's primary source; the story even flags 'not in fire'.)

statements.claim: The queens, led by Rukmini, embraced the body of Hari and entered the funeral fire.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt BP 11.31.14-24: 'the queens, led by Rukmini, entered the fire'; VP 5.38: 'The eight queens of Krishńa... with Rukminí at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire.' (BP verse 19 'rāma-patnyaś ca tad-deham upaguhyāgnim āviśan' covers the same embracing-the-body motif.)

statements.claim: Arjuna, grieving for his dearest friend Krishna, performed the funeral rites for the kinsmen whose family lines were destroyed.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.20-21: 'arjunaḥ preyasaḥ sakhyuḥ kṛṣṇasya virahāturaḥ / bandhūnāṃ naṣṭa-gotrāṇām arjunaḥ sāmparāyikam'.

statements.claim: The ocean — home of sharks and alligators — flooded over Dwaraka and its wealth; whatever ground the fleeing people passed the ocean covered immediately behind them, and the people said 'Wonderful is the course of fate.'
statements.evidence: MBh 16.7: 'the ocean, that home of sharks and alligators, flooded Dwaraka... Whatever portion of the ground was passed over, ocean immediately flooded over... the inhabitants of Dwaraka walked faster and faster, saying, "Wonderful is the course of fate!"' BP 11.31.22: 'dvārakāṃ hariṇā tyaktāṃ samudro 'plāvayat kṣaṇāt'.

statements.claim: The sea refused to take the Lord's own dwelling, which stood above the water and was never washed away; Keshava constantly abides there, and whoever visits that holy shrine is freed from all his sins.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwáraká, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu. The sea has not yet been able to wash that temple away, and there Keśava constantly abides... Whoever visits that holy shrine, the place where Krishńa pursued his sports, is liberated from all his sins.' BP 11.31.23: 'nityaṃ sannihitas tatra bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ'.

statements.claim: The Sudharman assembly hall and the Parijata tree, the two heavenly gifts Krishna brought down to Dwaraka, returned to heaven.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'The Sudharman palace and the Párijáta tree, which had been brought to earth by Krishńa, both proceeded to heaven.'

statements.claim: On the same day Hari departed from the earth the powerful dark-bodied Kali age descended.
statements.evidence: VP 5.38: 'on the same day that Hari departed from the earth the powerful dark-bodied Kali age descended.'

statements.claim: Arjuna led the surviving women, children and elders to Indraprastha and installed Vajra, the surviving heir of the Vrishnis, as king.
statements.evidence: BP 11.31.24: 'strī-bāla-vṛddhān ādāya hata-śeṣān dhanañjayaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'Arjuna, leading the surviving women, children and elders to Indraprastha, installed Vajra as king.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva had carried his newborn son through a stormy night to safety, and Devaki had lost her first children to a tyrant's fear.
statements.evidence: Backstory connective tissue from the corpus chain (Krishna's birth/escape episodes, earlier stories); not asserted in this pack's BP 11.31 passage but consistent with the series' established narrative.

notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. Source variant handled correctly: BP 11.31 (primary, conf 5) has Devaki/Rohini/Vasudeva die of grief, VP 5.38 (conf 4) has them enter the flames; the story follows BP and states this choice ('not in fire'). Arjuna 'as he had been summoned' references the Daruka-summons of MBh 16.4, present elsewhere in the pack corpus.

statements.claim: After the Yadava slaughter Krishna, before his own end, returned to Dwaraka one final time; the city's men were gone and only women, children and the old remained.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: Krishna tells Rama to wait 'till I place the ladies under the care of kinsmen', then 'Entering the city of Dwaravati, Janardana said these words unto his father'; context of the universal Yadava slaughter at Prabhasa.

statements.claim: Krishna had sent his charioteer Daruka to the Kurus with news of the slaughter and a summons for Arjuna to come quickly.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Krishna commanded Daruka, saying, "Going to the Kurus, inform Partha of this great slaughter of the Yadus. Let Arjuna come here quickly."'

statements.claim: Krishna watched Vabhru, the last survivor of the Yadavas, slain by the iron bolt that pursued the cursed clan to the end.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'the iron-bolt... suddenly sprang of itself upon that solitary survivor of the Yadava race and slew him... Beholding Vabhru slain, Keshava... addressed his elder brother.'

statements.claim: Balarama waited for Krishna at the edge of the forest while Krishna went into the city.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Do thou, O Rama, wait for me here till I place the ladies under the care of kinsmen'; Krishna later: 'At the skirts of the forest Rama is waiting for me. I shall meet him today.'

statements.claim: Krishna told Vasudeva: 'Protect all the ladies of our house, until Dhananjaya comes... At the skirts of the forest, Rama is waiting for me. I shall meet him today. I have beheld this great carnage of the Yadavas, just as I beheld the carnage of the foremost Kshatriyas of Kuru's race. It is impossible for me to see this city of the Yadavas without the Yadavas beside me. Know that I am going to the woods, to practise penances with Rama in my company.'
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4, near-verbatim: 'Do thou protect all the ladies of our house, till Dhananjaya comes... This great carnage of the Yadus has been beheld by me even as I beheld before the carnage of those Kshatriyas who were the foremost ones of Kuru's race... Know that proceeding to the woods I shall practise penances with Rama in my company.'

statements.claim: Krishna touched his father's feet with his head and left quickly.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Krishna touched the feet of his father with his head, and quickly left his presence.'

statements.claim: A loud wail rose from the ladies and children of the house; Krishna retraced his steps and told the weeping women: 'Arjuna will come here. That foremost of men will relieve you of your grief.'
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Then a loud wail of sorrow arose from the ladies and children of his house... Keshava retraced his foot-steps and said unto them, "Arjuna will come here. That foremost of men will relieve you of your grief."'

statements.claim: Krishna walked out of Dwaraka for the last time toward the forest where his elder brother sat in solitude, and toward the end waiting for him beneath a tree.
statements.evidence: MBh 16.4: 'Proceeding then to the forest, Keshava beheld Rama sitting in a solitary spot thereof'; the 'end beneath a tree' anticipates the Jara episode (BP 11.30 / MBh 16.4) in the corpus chain.

notes: Near-verbatim MBh 16.4. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. The framing (task as the gift that holds a man upright, farewells that last too long) is connective interpretation only.

statements.claim: The asura Vrikasura, son of Shakuni, met the sage Narada on the road.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.13: 'vṛko nāmāsuraḥ putraḥ śakuneḥ pathi nāradam'.

statements.claim: Narada told Vrikasura: 'Worship Girisha, the god of the mountain. Do that, and you will succeed quickly.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.14: 'sa āha devaṃ giriśam upādhāvāśu siddhyasi'.

statements.claim: Vrikasura went to Kedara, the mountain shrine of Shiva, and performed a terrible penance.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.16: 'ity ādiṣṭas tam asura upādhāvat sva-gātrataḥ' (worshipped with his own body, i.e., austerity); location Kedara given in pack index entry.

statements.claim: For seven days the god did not appear; on the seventh day, out of despair, the most compassionate Shiva rose before him like fire rising from fire and said: 'Enough. Choose a boon from me. Whatever you wish, I will give it to you.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.17-19: 'devopalabdhim aprāpya nirvedāt saptame 'hani / tadā mahā-kāruṇiko sa dhūrjaṭir... cāgnir ivotthito 'nalāt / tam āha... alaṃ vṛṇīṣva me yathābhikāmaṃ vitarāmi te varam'.

statements.claim: Vrikasura asked the boon that whoever's head he touched should die.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.20: 'devaṃ sa vavre pāpīyān varaṃ bhūta-bhayāvaham'; pack excerpt: 'the boon that whomever he touches on the head shall die.'

statements.claim: Shiva was displeased but granted it reluctantly, and a boon once offered cannot be taken back.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.21: 'tac chrutvā bhagavān rudro durmanā iva bhārata' (as if displeased); the irrevocability gloss is the standard force of the boon-grammar in the episode.

statements.claim: To test the boon, Vrikasura tried to place his hand on Shiva's own head.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.22: 'sa tad-vara-parīkṣārthaṃ śambhor mūrdhni kilāsuraḥ'.

statements.claim: Terrified and trembling, Shiva fled, pursued by the demon across the earth to its ends and through the heavens; the lords of the gods watched in silence, knowing no counter-measure.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.23-24: 'tenopasṛṣṭaḥ santrastaḥ parādhāvan sa-vepathuḥ / ajānantaḥ prati-vidhiṃ tūṣṇīm āsan sureśvarāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'flees to the ends of the earth and heavens.'

statements.claim: Shiva took refuge in Vaikuntha, the abode of Narayana, the supreme goal of renunciates, where the Lord sat blazing like fire — with sacred thread/girdle, deerskin, staff and prayer beads — the destroyer of affliction, who had seen the god's distress.
statements.evidence: BP 10.88.25-27: 'yatra nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣān nyāsināṃ paramo gatiḥ / taṃ tathā vyasanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavān vṛjinārdanaḥ / mekhalājina-daṇḍākṣais tejasāgnir iva jvalan'.

statements.claim: When a demon practices self-denial he is not seeking purity but power; Vrikasura had never once been told no.
statements.evidence: Interpretive characterization consistent with the episode (the boon sought is bhūta-bhayāvaha, fear for all beings); pack does not state motives beyond the actions.

notes: Faithful to BP 10.88.12-27. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED. Rendering 'mekhalā' as 'sacred thread' is a translation-level word choice, not a factual deviation.
